How a Detailed AGENT.md Turns My MacBook Into a Surprisingly Capable Development Team

17 min read
1 hour ago

--

Press enter or click to view image in full size

The cloud handles architecture, AGENT.md carries the decisions, and the Mac handles implementation. Image by author.AI coding agents are very good at starting projects.
Finishing them is a different story.
Give an AI model a vague prompt such as “build me a web application,” and it will immediately start producing code. It will choose a framework, invent a database schema, create a few components, and confidently march in whatever direction seems reasonable at that exact moment.
Sometimes that direction is even correct.
My first experiments with local coding models often followed this pattern. The model would produce code quickly, but after a few iterations the project would start to drift. A component used one naming convention, the API used another, and a feature I considered essential had quietly disappeared somewhere around prompt number twelve.
The model was not necessarily bad at coding. It simply did not have a good plan.
So I stopped asking one model to do everything. Instead, I use powerful cloud models such as ChatGPT and Claude to plan the project. I then give that plan to a smaller model running locally on my MacBook and let it handle most of the…
